To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) SNe Ia in older galaxies are brighter than average, after standard light-curves corrections, and (b) SNe Ias in more massive galaxies are brighter than SNe Ias that occur in less massive galaxies, after standard lightcurve corrections.
SNe Ia in more massive and older host galaxies are brighter than average.
the residuals of SNIa about the best-fitting Hubble diagram correlate with both the mass-weighted ages and stellar masses of their host galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the estimates of the stellar masses and mass-weighted ages of SN Ia host galaxies.
improving the accuracy with which the stellar mass and average age of SN Ia host galaxies are measured.
improving the estimates of the stellar masses and mass-weighted ages of Type Ia SN host galaxies by combining ultraviolet, optical, and near-infrared (NIR) photometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most massive and oldest host galaxies tend to host SNe Iae that are brighter than the average SN Ia.
the most massive and oldest galaxies in the local Universe host the brightest SNe Ia.
SNe Ia in younger galaxies are fainter than average after light-curve corrections, but the effect is smaller than that of the host-galaxy mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the properties of the SN Ia host galaxy, as measured by stellar mass and average age, can account for a significant fraction of the scatter about the Hubble diagram.
SNe Ia in younger galaxies are brighter than average, whereas those in older galaxies are fainter than average, but that more massive galaxies tend to host brighter SNe.
more massive, older galaxies host brighter SNe, but the trend with age alone is not as strong as the trend with stellar mass alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host galaxy stellar mass and massweighted average age are two of the most important properties that correlate with SN Ia properties.

the host-galaxy properties of SNe Ias in our sample are not well described by the stellar mass of the host galaxy alone, and that the mass-weighted age of the stellar populations in these galaxies can be used to improve our understanding of the progenitor systems of SNe I.
SNe Ia are better standardizable candles when their host-galaxy properties are accounted for.
